subject.title: Low-risk: Docker Go template injection, thread-ownership URL path injection, TLS env bypass

question: Should OpenClaw keep the documented private-DNS WebSocket and Control UI break-glass knobs as operator-controlled policy, narrow them now, or split only the non-policy input-validation fixes first?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve the Gateway break-glass behavior, while the Docker and thread-ownership fixes are narrower input-validation hardening; automation should not choose the security and compatibility tradeoff alone.

options.title: Split narrow fixes first
options.body: Land Docker label validation and thread URL encoding in a focused repair while keeping the Gateway and Control UI break-glass policy change behind explicit maintainer security review.

options.title: Narrow all break-glass paths
options.body: Replace hostname-wide private WebSocket allowance and broad Control UI dangerous flags with narrower mechanisms, accepting the docs, tests, and possible operator upgrade impact.

options.title: Keep current break-glass policy
options.body: Treat the Gateway and Control UI behavior as intentional operator policy and only take Docker/thread hardening if maintainers agree those helper boundaries should be stricter.

recommendation.title: Split narrow fixes first
recommendation.body: Land Docker label validation and thread URL encoding in a focused repair while keeping the Gateway and Control UI break-glass policy change behind explicit maintainer security review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest history across private WebSocket policy, caller/docs propagation, and related gateway security surface.
